# YM48: 紫碧山房 Zibi Shanfang, "The Cold Hill, Han Shan"

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM48` · Page: `/scenes/#YM48` · Row: `research/buildings/YM48-zibi-shanfang/`

## What it was

紫碧山房 Zibi Shanfang, north-west of the rear wall of 鸿慈永祜, on the highest hill of the garden: front hall 横云堂 Hengyun Tang, 石帆室 in a rock cave east of the main hall, 丰乐轩 south-east, 霁华楼 north, 景晖楼 further east, 澄素楼 on the pool west of 横云堂, 引溪亭 north-west (S05 j81:25a). Enlarged about 1760; 景晖楼 three storeys; main hall five bays with eave plaque 乐在人和; after 1860 the inner gate, the main hall and a pavilion survived under guard and were lost around 1900 (E2315, S361; S05 j81:25b). Malone's Han Shan 'Cold Hill', climbed on the ninth of the ninth moon (E2314, S02). 刘敦桢's 1933 list of 17 buildings left after 1860 includes 紫碧山房 and 顺木天 (E0451, S337).

From the inventory row: **built** after 1744, date unknown (not in the album); 1760; **changed** c. 1760 rebuilt; **destroyed** 1860; on the 1873 survival list (S06); survived 1860; later loss; inner gate, 乐在人和, 顺木天 survived 1860; lost around 1900 (S05, S02, S41, S06, S01, S337, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not one of the Forty Scenes of 1744.

### How later sources differ

Enlarged in 1760 after the second southern tour (E2316, E2315); a Jiaqing note of 1817 puts it in the north-west corner over the rice fields, with new barracks added near it in 1814 (S360, under 澄素楼).

## What survives today

The 2017 dig at 紫碧山房, the high north-west corner of the garden, found the duty rooms, gate, main hall, 含余清 and 澄素楼, a landing stage, a stone bridge, walls, paths, the stream, the hill and drains, and features no text records: an earlier wall base, hill retaining walls, a half-round landing and flagstone paths (S132). No figures in metres published in what was seen.

Dug in 2017: a service house, the gate, the halls 紫碧山房, 含余清 and 澄素楼, a landing, a stone bridge, walls, roads, a channel and the hill, plus an earlier wall footing, a hill retaining wall and a semicircular landing not in the documents (E2318, S132).
